moc.chu: Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp discovered Comet Hale–Bopp separately on July 23, 1995, before it became visible to the naked eye.
Hale–Bopp had its closest approach to Earth on March 22, 1997, at a distance of 1.315 AU (196.72 million km; 122.24 million mi).
As it passed perihelion on April 1, 1997, the comet developed into a spectacular sight.
Its massive nucleus size made it visible to the naked eye for a record 18 months.
Accordingly, Hale–Bopp was dubbed the Great Comet of 1997.
